description: Configuration for the model as PROPOSER in offline domain learning (eval/learn_family.py), not as executor. The model, its hash and the llama.cpp build are executor_config.json's. Two things differ. The sampled draws are cooler, temperature 0.2 against the executor's 0.85: a proposal is one careful answer, not one of twenty for a pass@k ladder. And the greedy context is 32,768 tokens, because the proposer's prompt holds the whole domain, about 17,000 tokens, and does not fit the executor's 16,384. Nothing measured with the executor uses this file.

runtime.conda_channel: defaults (repo.anaconda.com/pkgs/main); conda-forge ships only a CPU build for macOS
runtime.backend_note: The Metal backend is a loadable module in the env's bin/, not lib/. It is loaded from backend_dir before the model; without it llama.cpp silently falls back to the CPU.

load.note: How the file is read from disk; neither changes the numerics. load_mode is pinned rather than left on auto, which resolved to mmap on this machine.

context.flash_attn_note: Pinned rather than left on auto. On this build auto resolves to disabled for this model, because the Metal backend reports Flash Attention unsupported for it.

sampling.note: Argmax only: no temperature, top-k/top-p, penalties, DRY, grammar or speculative drafting. Greedy single-sequence decoding is what makes the output reproducible (LLM_RTL_code_generation.md 9.8). The pass@k ladder uses a separate, seeded sampled configuration.

ladder_sampling.memory_note: The unified cache holds the prompt once plus max_new_tokens per sequence: n_prompt + P * max_new_tokens cells. If that would exceed max_context_tokens, fewer sequences are decoded at a time. 45,056 cells is about 11 GB of f16 cache for this model, plus a compute buffer that grows with the cache: about 47 GB with the 32.4 GB of weights, under the 53 GB Metal working set. Version 3: before it, the cache was sized parallel_sequences * (n_prompt + max_new_tokens), and VerilogEval's Prob147 ran the GPU out of memory.
ladder_sampling.chain: temperature, then top-p, then a seeded draw (the OpenAI and Hugging Face order); sample i of a request is seeded base_seed + i
ladder_sampling.note: For proposals only. The executor's chain with a lower temperature: temperature, then top-p, then a seeded draw; sample i of a request is seeded base_seed + i.

generation.extraction: the last fenced ```verilog block of the reply; a reply without one is an abstention

machine.note: Greedy outputs are only expected to be byte-identical on this machine, OS and build. GPU kernels are not batch-invariant, so another chip or a macOS/Metal update can change them; record any change here.
